subtype: Approach: checking the budget with a parent and trimming [Revision]
passage:
Monday. Dolma wrote the party list: balloons, return gifts, cake. At the stationery shop and the bakery, Dolma noted each price on the back of a copybook.

Wednesday. Dolma showed the numbers to Ama. She counted the money in the envelope she had set aside and shook her head. "This is more than we can spend, Dolma." Dolma stared at the page, then crossed out the fancy gift bags. "Small pencil sets instead. And I'll cut coloured paper for the decorations."

Saturday. Paper chains hung across the room. The pencil sets went home in twelve hands, and Ama's envelope still had a little money left.

qa.q: What did Dolma give the guests as return gifts in the end?
How did Dolma feel when Ama shook her head over the prices?
qa.a: Dolma was probably disappointed, since Dolma stared at the page in silence before crossing out the fancy gift bags, but Dolma stayed practical. 😔

qa.q: What alternative approach could Dolma use to plan the spending, and why?
qa.a: Dolma could set the limit first and choose what fits inside it, since deciding the total before shopping avoids the shock of adding it up later.

qa.q: How might Ama see Dolma's changes to the plan?
qa.a: Ama likely sees a child who listened and worked with a limit; the envelope had money left, so Ama may feel relieved and proud.

grounding: When the costs exceed the envelope, the child checks with Ama and trims the return gifts and decorations to fit.

subtype: Approach: checking the budget with a parent and trimming [Revision]
passage: Disha, you want everything for your party, na? Let your Jyoti Bua tell you about my tenth birthday. I made a big list: balloons, a cream cake, and return gifts, those shiny boxes with toys inside. I took it to my Papa, and he sat down with me and added it all up. Then he showed me the envelope he'd kept for the party. The list came to more than the envelope. I sulked for one whole evening. The next day I sat with the list again. The shiny boxes went; instead, small pencil sets, two pencils and an eraser each. The balloons stayed, but the paper chains and stars I cut myself from coloured paper. My friends still talk about those stars.

qa.q: What did young Jyoti choose instead of the shiny boxes?
qa.a: Small pencil sets, two pencils and an eraser each.

qa.q: How did young Jyoti feel when the list came to more than the envelope?
qa.a: She felt disappointed and sulked for a whole evening before coming back to the list.

qa.q: What was the turning point in the story, and why did it work?
qa.a: Going back to the list the next day and trimming it, swapping the boxes for pencil sets and making decorations herself, so the party fit the envelope.

qa.q: How might Jyoti's Papa have seen her trimmed list?
qa.a: Papa had added it up with her, so seeing her make the cuts herself may have made him proud.

grounding: Shows a child whose party costs exceed what a parent set aside, trimming return gifts to pencil sets and making paper decorations at home.

subtype: Approach: checking the budget with a parent and trimming [Revision]
passage: Two days before his party, Anand sat with Mummy at the kitchen table and added up his list: balloons, a chocolate cake from the bakery, and twelve toy cars as return gifts. Mummy showed him the amount she had put aside. The list was well over it, and the bakery needed the cake order by that evening. Anand's face fell. Then he picked up the pencil. "Cake stays. Balloons, only one packet." He crossed out the toy cars. "Little pencil sets instead. And Samir and I can make the decorations." That night, as shop shutters came down in the lane, Anand and his brother Samir sat on the floor cutting coloured-paper chains, tongues out in concentration.

qa.q: What did Anand want as return gifts at first?
How did Anand feel when he saw the list was over the amount?
qa.a: His face fell, so he felt disappointed, before picking up the pencil to rethink the list.

qa.q: What could Anand do if the list were still a little over?
qa.a: Talk it through again with Mummy and keep what matters most; cutting the gifts and making decorations at home already brought it closer.

qa.q: What might making decorations be like for Samir?
qa.a: Samir gets to sit on the floor cutting paper chains with Anand, which seems fun and makes him part of the party.

grounding: Illustrates a boy checking party costs with his mother, finding them over her set amount, and trimming gifts to pencil sets and home-made decorations.
